name: Blockchain Oracles
description: Oracles solve the 'oracle problem': smart contracts on-chain cannot natively access off-chain data (real-world prices, weather, sports results, API responses). Oracle networks act as trusted middleware between blockchains and the external world. Covers hybrid smart contracts that combine on-chain logic with off-chain data, Chainlink as the dominant oracle provider, and oracle network architectures (decentralized, first-party, layer-2 oracle solutions).

subskills.name: Hybrid Smart Contracts
subskills.description: Smart contracts that combine tamper-proof on-chain code with off-chain oracle data, computation, or services to produce applications impossible with either component alone. Examples: DeFi price feeds (on-chain lending protocol + off-chain price data), parametric insurance (on-chain policy + off-chain weather API), dynamic NFTs (on-chain token + off-chain real-world event), verifiable random functions (VRF) for on-chain randomness. Understanding the trust boundary between on-chain and off-chain components is critical.

subskills.name: Chainlink
subskills.description: Chainlink is the dominant decentralized oracle network. Key products: Data Feeds (aggregated price feeds for DeFi, sourced from multiple nodes), VRF v2 (verifiable random function for provably fair randomness in NFTs, games), Automation (Keepers — automated smart contract execution based on conditions), CCIP (Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol — secure token and message bridging), Functions (arbitrary off-chain computation). Chainlink's node operator network, reputation system, and LINK token economics. Integration patterns using AggregatorV3Interface.

subskills.name: Oracle Networks & Alternatives
subskills.description: The broader oracle landscape beyond Chainlink: Pyth Network (first-party price feeds from institutional publishers, sub-second latency, push-based), Band Protocol (cross-chain oracle), API3 (first-party oracles — data providers run their own nodes, eliminating intermediaries), Tellor (decentralized, dispute-based oracle), UMA (optimistic oracle for arbitrary off-chain data claims). Oracle attack vectors: flash loan price manipulation, oracle staleness exploits (Compound COMP price), single-source oracle failures. The oracle selection decision: latency requirements, data source trust, economic security.
